premises.text: Parents' anxiety about SIDS and breathing emergencies is poorly served by current monitors that do not actually tell whether a baby is breathing
premises.evidence_span: the current monitors on the market stink. They're old, they're outdated, and they don't actually tell you if your baby is breathing or not

premises.text: Owlet smart sock sends heart rate and oxygen (plus related vitals) to a smartphone and alerts parents in emergencies using pulse-oximetry technology
premises.evidence_span: It's a smart sock that sends heart rate and oxygen levels to a parent's smartphone and can alert you in case of an emergency

premises.text: Electronics are flexible, silicone-encased, and waterproof so the sock is baby-proof
premises.evidence_span: we've made the electronics completely flexible, and we've encased it in silicone so that it is also waterproof

premises.text: Multiple sensors provide many light/receiver combinations so readings stay reliable as an infant's foot triples in size in the first year
premises.evidence_span: With four sensors, we're getting nine different combinations, and we're getting a great reading the whole time

premises.text: Aggregated infant health data can enable predictions from common colds to more life-threatening conditions beyond hospital discharge
premises.evidence_span: creating the largest data set of infant health data that's ever been known

value.text: Parents are empowered to protect infant health with real-time vitals alerts that can help save babies' lives
value.evidence_span: It's gonna empower parents and it's gonna improve the health of infants all over the world

secondary_value.text: Building predictive insights from continuous infant vitals data after hospital discharge
secondary_value.evidence_span: we could come up with any predictions from anything from the common cold to things that are more life-threatening

causal_links.evidence_span: anything that saves a baby's life is worth it
getting push notifications, for example, if your baby didn't sleep very well the night before, or if they're really warm, or even if they're just awake, is very helpful and empowering for parents
we're really excited because we could come up with any predictions from anything from the common cold to things that are more life-threatening
